title: Continuity of bounded-below cohomology of oriented etale products
statement:
Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(X_i\to S_i\leftarrow Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of diagrams of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, with quasi-compact quasi-separated arrows [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume all three component transition morphisms are affine (inverse images of affine opens are affine). Let $X,S,Y$ be the componentwise inverse limits and put
$$P_i=(X_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(S_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}}(Y_i)_{\mathrm{Et}},\qquad P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$$
using the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and left oriented products [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Write $u_{ji}:P_j\to P_i$ and $u_i:P\to P_i$ for the induced geometric morphisms. Fix $i_0\in I$, a commutative ring $\Lambda$, and $K\in D^+(P_{i_0},\Lambda)$, the bounded-below derived category of sheaves of constant-$\Lambda$ modules [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every integer $n$, the canonical pullback maps give an isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_{(a:j\to i_0)\in(I/i_0)^{\mathrm{op}}} H^n(R\Gamma(P_j,u_{ji_0}^*K))\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ H^n(R\Gamma(P,u_{i_0}^*K)).$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is total right derived global sections, computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and the pullbacks are the exact constant-coefficient inverse images. The isomorphism is natural in $K$ and commutes with restriction along a morphism of such inverse systems and with the adjunction-unit maps defining cohomological pullback. No torsion, constructibility or finite-dimensional hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), localization (1.b)–(1.c), and 2.5–2.7, especially the inverse limits and their cohomology comparisons (2.c)–(2.e), printed pp. 175–176, 179–181. General affine-transition form of this continuity input; the finite-cover site cohomology theorem is Stacks sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), with sites.tex Tag 09YL (lemma-colimit-sites).

proof.text: Put $J=I/i_0$ and let $r:J\to I$ forget the arrow to $i_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion], $J$ is small cofiltered and $r$ is initial: any $i\in I$ has a common predecessor $j$ with $i_0$, giving an arrow $r(j\to i_0)\to i$; any two such arrows from one object become equal after a refinement in $I$, which is also a refinement in $J$ by composition with its fixed arrow to $i_0$. The same criterion, applied with opposite target category, preserves the three component limits. Hence we may work over $J$; its opposite is exactly the filtered category in the asserted formula. The identity arrow of $i_0$ is the distinguished stage, and the composite pullback to $P$ is $u_{i_0}^*$.

source.place: Tags 04E6 (definition-cofinal), 04E7 (lemma-cofinal), and 002R (lemma-initial); applied to the slice projection.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-oriented-triple-limit-descent] on this system. Its first clause supplies qcqs limits and arrows, so [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation] supplies finite-cover triple sites with terminal triples and restriction equivalences to the $P_j$ and $P$. Its second clause provides strict small site models $\mathcal C_j$, $\mathcal C$ with finite coverings, cover-preserving continuous transition functors, and colimiting object and arrow cocones. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]; its canonical site morphisms agree with $u_{ji}$ and $u_i$ by the third clause of the new node. Thus its inverse-image formula and the abstract cohomology-colimit theorem can be used on the actual oriented products, including their canonical maps, rather than on unrelated equivalent topoi.

source.place: XI 2.5 and 2.7 (2.c), printed pp. 179–180; the finite-cover site colimit is Stacks sites.tex, Tags 09YL and 0A35.

proof.text: Work first with abelian sheaves. For $F$ on $P_{i_0}$ set $F_j=u_{ji_0}^{-1}F$ and $F_\infty=u_{i_0}^{-1}F$. The inverse-image composition comparisons identify every $u_j^{-1}F_j$ with $F_\infty$ and all transitions with its identity. Therefore their colimit is $F_\infty$ by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites] with the terminal triple at the distinguished stage; base change takes that triple to each terminal triple. We obtain $\varinjlim_{J^{\mathrm{op}}} H^p(P_j,F_j)\cong H^p(P,F_\infty)$ for $p\ge0$, with the adjunction-unit pullback maps specified in that node. By [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] these are the groups of $R\Gamma(F[0])$; [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] gives zero in negative degrees. Thus the comparison is proved for a sheaf in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), with derived.tex Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing) for negative degrees.

proof.text: For any geometric morphism $f$ in the system, its derived cohomological pullback is $R\Gamma(\eta_f)$ followed by the canonical composition identification $R\Gamma Rf_*\cong R\Gamma$. The source categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the constant integer sheaf for abelian sheaves. K-injective resolutions exist by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Right derived functors are triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], and exact inverse images induce triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The derived unit commutes with shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift], and [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] fixes the composition comparison to the actual composite adjunction. Consequently the canonical pullback transformation commutes with shifts: the unit and composition maps are unchanged when the chosen resolutions are shifted. Its naturality on all three arrows of a distinguished triangle, including the shifted last arrow, makes a morphism of triangles. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] it therefore gives a morphism of long exact cohomology sequences.

source.place: Right derived functors and triangulated functors, together with the canonical adjunction normalization of the cited nodes; XI 2.7 (*) identifies the comparison as the functoriality map.

proof.text: Let $L\in D^+(P_{i_0},\mathbb Z)$ and choose $a$ with $\mathcal H^q(L)=0$ for $q<a$. We prove by induction on $b-a+1$ that the canonical comparison for $\tau_{\le b}L$ is an isomorphism in every degree. The base $b=a-1$ is the zero object: all its cohomology vanishes. For $b\ge a$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] gives the functorial triangle $\tau_{\le b-1}L\to\tau_{\le b}L\to\mathcal H^b(L)[-b]\to$. Exact inverse image commutes with its kernels, images and quotients, hence with its truncations and cohomology sheaves; apply the exact derived functor from the preceding step. After derived sections the preceding step gives compatible long exact sequences at every stage and at the limit. Taking their filtered colimit keeps them exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. The induction hypothesis and step 3, shifted by $-b$, give isomorphisms for the first and third vertices in all degrees. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] to each five-term segment with the middle group belonging to $\tau_{\le b}L$. This proves the induction claim, for all degrees, without a bound on the cohomological dimension of the sites.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle); exactness of filtered colimits and the five lemma are used as the cited generic tools.

proof.text: Fix the required integer $n$. The functor $\Gamma$ is additive left exact, so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] applies on every stage site and the limit site: the inclusion $\tau_{\le n}L\to L$ induces an isomorphism on $H^nR\Gamma$. Exact inverse image identifies these inclusions with the pullbacks of the distinguished-stage inclusion. The natural comparison square thus has three isomorphisms, the top one from step 5 when $n\ge a$. If $n<a$, both sides vanish by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing]. This proves the abelian-complex continuity comparison for every integer $n$. In particular no infinite spectral-sequence passage or inverse-image preservation of injectives has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), parts (1) and (2): derived sections are left t-exact and degree n sees only the upper truncation at n.

proof.text: For the given constant ring $\Lambda$, let $V$ forget the module action. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], $Vu_i^*\cong u_i^{-1}V$, with the same adjunction units and composition comparisons. By [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget], evaluation at each terminal triple gives $vR\Gamma(K)\cong R\Gamma(VK)$, compatibly with the canonical global-cohomology pullbacks. Thus step 6 for $VK$ is exactly the underlying abelian-group comparison for the claimed module-cohomology map. A filtered colimit of modules has its underlying filtered colimit group, with action $\lambda[x]=[\lambda x]$; the equivalence relation respects the action because the transition maps are linear. The comparison is linear, and a bijective linear map has linear inverse, so the abelian isomorphism proves the required one for $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), extended to bounded-below derived evaluation as stated by the cited node.

proof.text: The isomorphism throughout is the original canonical map: step 3 uses the pullback via the adjunction unit, and steps 5–6 only test that map for invertibility. For a map of complexes, or a morphism of inverse systems, the underived squares commute because they apply the same inverse-image units and the same cocone coprojections. [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] supplies the naturality and composition identities on sheaves, and [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] supplies those same composite units on K-injective representatives. Naturality of units on complex morphisms and their composition identity therefore give these commuting squares already in the derived categories. Taking $H^n$, then the colimit, preserves the squares. The module comparisons of step 7 preserve the units as well, so the result is natural in $K$, commutes with restriction of inverse systems, and has the asserted adjunction-unit normalization. No coefficient torsion, constructibility, or dimension condition was used.

IsColimit in the functor category states the comparison and its naturality in every bounded-below complex; restriction_limitSquare records compatibility with morphisms and reindexings of inverse systems. All named helper laws belong to this canonical comparison and are listed in declarations.
